summary: Hidden stream-queueing in continuous coalescer causing burst p99s for short streaming requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed intermittent p95/p99 spikes specifically on short streaming requests (1-5 tokens per request) during a traffic shift window. Spikes manifested as long tail latencies (2-6s) and occasional 504s for the affected tenant.

Impact:
- ClippeHealth production: elevated p99 for streaming endpoints; several user-facing timeouts and degraded UX for chat snippets.
- Estimated affected request volume ~0.6% of total traffic but concentrated on high-value tenant routes.

Environment:
- Prod cluster: us-east serving fleet (dedicated shard for enterprise customers).
- Serving runtime version: v2026.02.18-rc3.
- Coalescer config: continuous-batcher enabled, max_batch_ms=15, max_batch_tokens=4096, tenant_weighting=true.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Run baseline steady-state mix: 60% long sequences (>=512 tokens) + 40% short streaming requests. Latency normal.
2) Shift workload quickly to 85% short streaming (spike of chat snippet traffic) over ~30s.
3) Observe continuous-batcher behavior: short requests are held pending coalescer while long sequences occupy slots; when long sequences begin to finish, a burst of short streams flush with increased queuing latency.

Observed metrics & logs (snippets):
- SLO graphs: https://graphs.redwood.com/clippers/streams/p99-2026-03-01.png
- Sample proxy logs: 
  [2026-03-01T14:22:07.123Z] tenant=clipper req_id=abc123 enqueue_time=14:22:07.123 coalescer_hold_ms=2100 flush_size=12
  [2026-03-01T14:22:07.124Z] tenant=clipper req_id=def456 downstream_start=14:22:09.234 downstream_latency_ms=3200 status=504
- Runtime trace: evidence of stream request staying in coalescer queue while GPU compute pipeline occupied by a few long batches.

Initial hypothesis:
- Continuous coalescer prioritization and tenant-weighted merging creates a hidden queue that allows short streams to accumulate behind long-sequence batches during sudden workload composition changes. When the coalescer flushes, the burst causes head-of-line delays visible as p99 spikes and occasional timeouts for streaming sessions.

Requested customer impact details:
- Customer provided a list of failed request IDs and approximate timestamps; support attached and correlated with cluster logs.

Workarounds attempted by Support before internal escalation:
- Temporary per-tenant rate-limit reduction for the short-stream route (reduced QPS by 20%).
- Applied a per-tenant config change to lower coalescer max_hold_ms to 5ms on a single shard as an experiment (reduced tail during trial but had broader throughput implications).

Next steps asked of SRE/Eng:
- Reproduce in staging with synthetic workload that transitions from long->short sequences rapidly.
- Add telemetry to coalescer to emit per-tenant queue depth and hold durations.
- Consider tenant-level safety valve: when short-stream fraction spikes, prefer immediate flush for streaming routes.
comments: 2026-03-01 15:02 - Support (Aisha): Customer reports repeated p99 spikes after traffic shift event at 14:20 UTC. Attached request ids + timelines. Marking P1 due to enterprise customer impact.

2026-03-01 16:10 - SRE (Marco): Confirmed cluster wide short-stream p99 increase overlapping timestamps. Root cause not yet identified. Kicked off staging replay job to reproduce with workload generator.

2026-03-01 18:34 - Eng (Priya Rao): Observed coalescer traces showing >2s hold for short streams while long sequence batches are draining. Hypothesis: coalescer chooses to wait to achieve economy-of-scale across tenants which backfires on short streaming sessions.
2026-03-02 09:12 - Support (Aisha): Customer applied temporary client-side retry/backoff; still saw degraded UX. Recommended keep connection open and wait for platform fix.
investigation_notes: Staging replay reproduced: synthetic mix with sudden short-heavy spike produced identical p99 tails when tenant_weighting enabled.
Disabling tenant_weighting in staging eliminated tail but increased per-token cost for long-sequence traffic (unacceptable default change).
Telemetry gap: coalescer did not previously emit per-tenant hold times; added lightweight span to trace hold_ms and flush_reason.
Patch candidate: introduce flush-priority for streaming routes and a per-tenant short-stream-fraction threshold to force immediate flush when exceeded.

Tested hotfix on a single prod shard at 2026-03-02 02:30 UTC: adjusted coalescer to prefer streaming flushes under threshold; p99 improved from ~3000ms to ~420ms for affected tenant with minimal impact on long-sequence throughput.
Follow-up: add dashboard for continuous-batcher hold-time per tenant + alert when short-stream fraction >60% and avg hold_ms > 250ms.
resolution:
Applied targeted hotfix (runtime PR #5894) to coalescer: streaming routes gain flush-priority when per-tenant short-stream fraction exceeds configurable threshold. Hotfix rolled to affected shard and then fleet. Customer confirmed p99 decreased to acceptable levels and timeouts stopped.

Post-incident actions:
- Backfilled telemetry to track per-tenant hold durations and flush reasons.
- Dedicated follow-up task: implement dynamic tenant safety valve and documentation of config knobs for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Engineering ticket created to evaluate long-term coalescer redesign to avoid head-of-line effects: INT-43102.
